svg.text: LLM Quantization: Running 70B Models on a Laptop
From FP32 to INT4: how reducing precision cuts memory 8x with minimal quality loss
Each format uses different bit widths to represent the same number. Fewer bits = less memory but less precision.
A 7B model needs 28 GB in FP32 but only 3.5 GB in INT4 -- datacenter vs laptop.
RTX 4090 (24GB) can run: 7B INT4, 13B INT4 | MacBook Pro M3 Max (64GB) can run: 70B INT4
Methods trade off speed, quality, and hardware compatibility.

As explained in our KV-cache deep dive, the cache grows with context length. Quantizing it provides additional savings.
Fits on a single A100 40GB with room to spare!
Key: INT4 is the sweet spot for local deployment (8x smaller, ~5% quality loss) | INT8 for production serving
FP16 when quality is critical | GGUF for CPU/mixed, AWQ/GPTQ for GPU-only
